With a quick snap of its webbed wings the basilospri weaves among the colossal mountain forests canopy. Th is vicious flying lizard is 
unsuited for long periods of flight, but with its talon tipped phalanges it can pounce and pierce creatures in an instant, while still using 
the long digits to climb and cling to the immense trees in which it makes its home. Preferring tree dwelling prey, the basilospri is one 
of the few predators that can pierce the armored carapace of a ricatrillisk. Th ese lizards are highly territorial, and will defend their 
hunting grounds from their own kind in aggressive aerial disputes that often leave the defeated assailant’s wings tattered to plummet 
to the forest floor. Leaving their broken rivals to the ground dwelling scavengers of the Wealdwoods to fi nish off.
Class - Reptilia • Genus Derived Evolution - Anolis • Niche - Generalist Aerial Carnivore 
Preyed upon by - Sacrissian, Skyelarx • Preys on - Aphistus, Calitross, Frondilli, Lexati, Ricatrillisk, Vinnirex, Ynnil

Hunters Sense Th e basilospri has Advantage on Wisdom

Canopy Stalker Th e basilospri has Advantage on Dexterity

Flight Mastery By beating its wings and springing its tail, the 
basilospri can leap vertically 20 ft. into the air without needing a 
running start.
Actions
Multiattack Th e basilospri makes two attacks, using Biting 
Beak, Phalanges Talons and Scaled Tail in any combination.
Biting Beak Melee Attack Roll: +6 to hit, reach 5ft., one target. 
Hit: 9 (1d10 + 4) Piercing damage. If the target has the Prone 
condition, the basilospri shakes its head violently, causing an 
additional 5 (1d10) Piercing damage.
Phalanges Talons Melee Attack Roll: +6 to hit, reach 5ft., one 
target. Hit: 11 (2d6 +4) Piercing damage. If the basilospri flies 
at least 15 ft. toward the target immediately before the hit,
the target takes an additional 7 (2d6) Piercing damage and 
if the target is a Medium or smaller creature it has the Prone 
condition.
Scaled Tail Melee Attack Roll: +4 to hit, reach 10ft., one target. Hit:
11 (2d8 +2) Bludgeoning damage. Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 14, 
one Medium or smaller creature that the basilospri successfully 
hit with its Scaled Tail attack. Failure: Th e target is pushed back 5 
ft. to an unoccupied space.

Encountering Deep in the woodlands among colossal trees, 
half eaten carcasses hang from high tree branches to signify the 
hunting grounds of basilospri. Often found in small groups of 
three to four individuals, these wily reptiles stare down from 
their perches watching for both prey and interlopers. With a 
piercing cry that echoes among the trees, they will aggressively 
dive at any that could make for an easy meal.
Needing only its tail to grip onto 
branches as well as steer during flight 
has caused the hind limbs to become 
nearly vestigial. The clawed tips now 
only used to manipulate their meals
With a powerful beak, hollowed bones 
and the nascant feather-like scales, the 
basilospri is developing many avian traits 
through convergent evolution
Talons tip each long and powerful phalanges, giving 
the creature the ability to climb trees and pierce 
thick hides
